A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2-Router research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably; v2 retains Appendices A–B and adds Appendix C.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing experiments on R2-Bench, generalization tests, component ablations, and measurements of compliance with token budgets.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds RouterArena evaluations, thinking-token routing results, system-prompt robustness testing, and an interpolation comparison.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 adapts routing to thinking-token budgets, whereas v1 controls output-token budgets. Appendix C.4 explicitly adopts PCHIP instead of piecewise linear interpolation. The encoder, prediction heads, loss, and discrete selection rule remain unchanged. The interpolation revision is incompletely integrated because Equation 9 still specifies linear interpolation.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on RouterArena's 8,400 queries across knowledge, math, domain, code, trivia, translation, and NLU categories, extending the empirical coverage beyond the retained six-source R2-Bench. Appendix C.3 also introduces a distinct scenario with heterogeneous model-specific system prompts.

E2.justification: The established routing baselines remain unchanged, and the new RouterArena results reuse MIRT and CARROT-L. The limited addition is Table 8's direct comparison between PLI and PCHIP interpolation, with PLI providing the reference for the newly adopted interpolator. Newly cited routers are not shown as additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces substantial additional protocols: exact-match RouterArena evaluation with Arena Scores, expanded reasoning-model pools and thinking budgets, training and testing under model-specific prompts, and interpolation evaluation at non-anchor budgets using eight anchors. These supplement the original R2-Bench experiments; the PDFs do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends validation with heterogeneous-system-prompt robustness testing and a PLI-versus-PCHIP analysis of prediction error and routing cost. The judge-free RouterArena evaluation also explicitly investigates dependence on LLM judging. These address additional questions beyond v1's retained encoder, predictor, judge-substitution, conciseness-prompt, and anchor-count analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Uncertainty entries in the retained tables are identical. Appendix C adds point estimates but describes no additional run counts, uncertainty estimators, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original results are retained, while Table 7 adds RouterArena category advantages of 4.1–8.1 points over CARROT-L. Appendix C.2 reports Arena Scores of 71.6 versus MIRT's 66.9 and CARROT-L's 63.9; C.3 adds prompt-robustness AUDC of 0.81 versus an unnamed best baseline's 0.76. Table 8 reports PLI/PCHIP prediction errors of 0.09/0.05 and QNC of 0.14/0.12. Appendix A also completes a numerical claim as 3%–21% compliance at budget 10, although unchanged Figure 8 shows 3%–5% for the listed sub-4B models.

T1.justification: Definitions 4.1–4.2, Theorem 4.3, its assumptions and proof, and Equations 1–9 are retained. The added discussion and interpolation comparison introduce no new formal definitions, derivations, or guarantees.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims first place on the public RouterArena leaderboard at acceptance. The central claims about curve-based routing, R2-Bench's contribution, and comparable quality at 4–5 times lower cost remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of the complementary roles of R2-Bench and the router, why queries requiring detailed answers should receive larger budgets, and how training captures system-prompt interactions. Appendix C.4 newly discusses non-convex quality–cost relationships and interpolation's accuracy/data-efficiency tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code URL, an example of profiling/training costs for adding Gemini 3 Pro Preview, thinking-budget API parameters, and system-prompt examples. It clarifies total-cost accounting and reports discrete 16-anchor routing for the main experiments. The introduction's training time changes from 20 to 30 minutes, matching the already-stated value in Section 5.4.

R1.justification: v2 adds BEST-Route, HW-Router, Privacy-preserving LLMs Routing, and SecureRouter to the cited literature. Section 2.2 briefly contrasts sampling-based routing and hardware-aware cost estimation with its budget-control approach, without substantially changing the paper's overall positioning.

P1.justification: Most wording and the main section sequence are retained. v2 inserts explanatory paragraphs, adds Appendix C with four subsections, introduces conflict-of-interest and acknowledgement text, updates the publication footer, and completes the truncated Appendix A sentence.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8 for RouterArena and interpolation results. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–6 retain their displays and content, with limited relocation and page/column reflow, including Figure 6 and Tables 4–5.

improvement.justification: The separate, judge-free RouterArena evaluation and new thinking-budget and system-prompt tests strengthen support for applicability beyond v1's R2-Bench experiments. Code-access information also improves documentation. These benefits are partly offset by inconsistent integration: Sections 4.3.3/C.4 claim discrete 16-anchor main results, while Section 6.4/Figure 7 retain variable-anchor linear interpolation, and Equation 9 remains linear despite adopting PCHIP. The new Appendix A compliance range also conflicts with Figure 8. The net improvement is therefore limited.
